hero.title: Poker basics
hero.lead: Meet the cards, understand the table and take your first seat with confidence. No poker knowledge needed.

deck.title: 52 cards, four suits
deck.lead: A standard deck has no jokers. Each suit has the same 13 ranks; no suit beats another.
deck.ace: An ace is usually highest. It can also be lowest in A–2–3–4–5. Q–K–A–2–3 is not a straight.

ladder.title: The best five cards win
ladder.lead: The list runs from weakest to strongest. Tap a hand to see its cards and what makes it strong.
ladder.hint: These are probabilities for a random five-card hand. Hold’em probabilities for the best five of seven cards differ. Royal flush is counted separately from other straight flushes here.

items.name: High card
items.description: With no combination, compare the highest card, then the next cards if tied.

items.name: One pair
items.description: Two cards of the same rank. The higher pair wins; equal pairs compare the other cards (kickers).

items.name: Two pair
items.description: Two different pairs. Compare the higher pair, then the lower pair, then the remaining card.

items.name: Three of a kind
items.description: Three cards of the same rank. The higher triple wins; compare the remaining cards if tied.

items.name: Straight
items.description: Five consecutive ranks, with any suits. The top card decides; A–2–3–4–5 is the lowest straight.

items.name: Flush
items.description: Five cards of one suit, not necessarily consecutive. Compare from the highest card down.

items.name: Full house
items.description: Three of a kind plus a pair. Compare the triple first, then the pair.

items.name: Four of a kind
items.description: Four cards of the same rank. Compare their rank, then the fifth card if tied.

items.name: Straight flush
items.description: Five consecutive cards of one suit. The highest card decides.

items.name: Royal flush
items.description: 10–J–Q–K–A of one suit. The strongest hand; no hand beats it.

actions.title: Six actions, one decision
actions.lead: When your turn comes in a betting round, act according to the current bet and your chips.

items.name: Check
items.when: Available when there is no outstanding bet for you to match.

items.name: Bet
items.meaning: Make the first bet of this round.
items.when: Available when nobody has bet yet.

items.name: Call
items.when: If an opponent put in 10 and you put in 0, you pay 10.

items.name: Raise
items.when: If the bet is 10 and you raise the total to 30, others must respond to the new amount.

items.name: Fold
items.when: Use it when you do not want to continue. Chips already committed stay in the pot.

items.name: All-in
items.when: You put in your entire stack (the chips in front of you). Extra bets can create a separate side pot; you can only win pots you contributed to.

blinds.title: Blinds, antes and the pot
blinds.lead: The pot is the total of all chips committed to this hand. Forced payments get the action started.
notes: The dealer button marks the dealer position and moves one seat clockwise for each new hand.
At a six-player table, the player to the dealer’s left pays the small blind; the next pays the big blind. Example: SB 5, BB 10.
An ante is an extra forced payment before the hand, when the rules require it. Everyone may pay, or in some games the big blind pays for the table.
Blinds and antes enter the pot. If everyone folds, the remaining player wins without showing cards.
blinds.potExample: Example: SB 5 + BB 10 = a starting pot of 15 chips (no ante).

flow.title: Hold’em: two cards to showdown
flow.lead: You have two private cards and five community cards that everyone can use. Choose your best five from these seven; you do not have to use both private cards.

steps.name: Preflop
steps.text: Everyone receives two private cards. The first betting round starts to the left of the big blind.

steps.name: Flop
steps.text: Three community cards are revealed. Betting starts with the first remaining player to the dealer’s left.

steps.name: Turn
steps.text: The fourth community card is revealed, followed by another betting round.

steps.name: River
steps.text: The fifth and final community card is revealed. The final betting round follows.

steps.name: Showdown
steps.text: If at least two players remain, hands are compared. The best five-card hand wins the pot. Identical hands split the pot. In this example, you have two aces and two kings.

position.title: Acting later means knowing more
position.lead: Position is when you make your decision relative to the other players in a betting round. It changes with the dealer button.

items.name: Early position
items.text: You act before most players. You have less information because you have not seen their decisions.

items.name: Middle position
items.text: You see some decisions, but players remain behind you. Consider both the bets ahead and the players still to act.

items.name: Late position
items.text: You act after seeing many other decisions. The dealer (button) acts last after the flop when still in the hand.

position.note: Preflop, the big blind has the last initial decision (a raise may send action around again). After the flop, the blind positions act early.

quizSection.title: Ready for your first hand?
quizSection.lead: Eight quick questions. Wrong answers help you learn too; read the explanation for each one.

quiz.q: How many cards are in a standard poker deck?
quiz.explain: A standard deck without jokers has four suits × 13 ranks: 52 cards.
Two pair beats one pair, even a pair of aces.
A flush ranks above a straight.
Four of a kind beats a full house, regardless of the triple or kicker rank.

quiz.q: There is no outstanding bet. How can you continue without committing chips?
quiz.explain: Check passes your turn without adding chips when no bet needs matching.

quiz.q: There is no ante; SB pays 5 and BB pays 10. What is the starting pot?
quiz.explain: The pot is the sum of contributions: 5 + 10 = 15.
The ace can act low in the lowest straight, but cannot bridge high ranks to low ranks in the middle.

quiz.q: What is the dealer button’s advantage after the flop in Hold’em?
options: Acts last when still in the hand
quiz.explain: Acting later lets you see other players’ decisions. It does not change your cards.
